recipes.name: WINGS
ingredients: Hot sauce of choice, to taste
1/2 tsp hot sauce (e.g., Louisiana Crystal, Texas Pete, or Tabasco)
instructions: For Cooking Methods:
for the Fried
Pat the drums and flats dry using paper towels, then generously salt all sides of the wings with salt. - 2 lb chicken wings - As needed kosher salt
Transfer the drums and flats onto a wire rack set in a sheet tray. Allow the wings to dry, uncovered, in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours or up to 24 hours. - 2 lb chicken wings

When ready to cook, add the oil to a high-walled skillet and preheat to 375 °F. Add the dry-brined chicken wings to the oil and fry for 5-8 minutes or until cooked through and golden brown. Make sure to keep the oil temperature between 350-375 °F. Transfer the cooked wings to a paper towel-lined sheet tray to cool slightly before serving with your sauce of choice. - 48 ml fry oil of choice - 2 lb chicken wings
For the Baked

Whisk together the baking powder and salt. Pat the drums and flats dry using paper towels, then generously season all sides of the wings with salt/baking powder mixture. - 1 tsp baking powder - 1 tsp kosher salt - 2 lb chicken wings
Transfer the drums and flats onto a wire rack set in a sheet tray. Allow the wings to dry, uncovered, in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours or up to 24 hours. - 2 lb chicken wings
When ready to bake, preheat the oven to 250 °F degrees.

Prepare a large rimmed baking sheet tray with a layer of aluminum foil, making sure the high reflective side faces up. Sprinkle an even layer of baking soda over the foil to prevent the oil from burning during the roasting process. Then, transfer the rack with the chicken wings to the lined sheet tray. - baking soda as needed (for dusting) - 2 lb chicken wings

Bake the wings for 20 minutes, then remove the wings from the oven. Increase the temperature to 475 °F (with convection fan on). Once preheated, place the wings back into the oven and bake for an additional 20-30 minutes. Make sure to flip the wings halfway through the second baking period for even browning. - 2 lb chicken wings
Serve immediately with your sauce of choice.
for the Grilled
Pat the drums and flats dry using paper towels, then generously salt all sides of the wings with salt. - 2 lb chicken wings - kosher salt as needed
Transfer the drums and flats onto a wire rack set in a sheet tray. Allow the wings to dry, uncovered, in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours or up to 24 hours. - 2 lb chicken wings

When ready to cook, preheat half the grill over high heat, leaving the other side of the grill for indirect cooking. Grease the grill grate with vegetable oil before adding the chicken. - vegetable oil as needed
Add the wings to the indirect side of the grill, then cover the grill with the lid and cook for 12-15 minutes or until the skin has turned pale and opaque. - 2 lb chicken wings

Flip the wings and optionally, brush the wings with Barbecue Sauce. Continue cooking, occasionally turning and brushing with sauce (if using), for an additional 15-20 minutes. - 2 lb chicken wings - Optional: barbecue sauce (see sauces)
Increase the heat on the indirect side to medium-high and cook for an additional 3-5 minutes or until the wings are charred. - 2 lb chicken wings
Serving immediately with the sauce of choice.
For Sauces:
For the Buffalo Sauce Method
Combine all ingredients and set aside. - ½ cup hot sauce of choice - 6 tbsp unsalted butter melted - ½ tsp Worcestershire sauce - ⅛ tsp garlic powder - ⅛ tsp cayenne powder
For the Honey Dijon Sauce Method
Combine all ingredients and set aside until ready to use. - 3 tbsp Dijon mustard - 3 tbsp yellow mustard - ¼ cup honey - Hot sauce of choice to taste
For the Barbecue Sauce Method

In a medium saucepan, combine all the ingredients and bring to a bare simmer over medium-low heat. Reduce heat to low and cook, stirring frequently, until flavors have melded, 15 to 20 minutes. Add more water if the sauce becomes too thick, and if too thin, cook down to a thicker consistency. - ½ cup ketchup - ¼ cup water (more as needed) - 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar - 2 tsp Worcestershire sauce - 2 tsp yellow mustard - ½ tsp hot sauce (e.g. Louisiana Crystal, Texas Pete, or Tabasco) - 1 garlic clove minced or grated - ¼ cup packed brown sugar - 1 tsp smoked paprika - 1 tsp onion powder - ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
Set aside until ready to use or allow the sauce to cool to room temperature, then refrigerate until ready to use, up to 2 weeks.
For the Gochujang Sauce Method

Combine all of the ingredients, save for the sesame seeds, in a small sauce pot. Whisk to combine the ingredients and cook over medium heat for 10-15 minutes or until thickened. - ⅓ cup Gochujang - ¼ cup water - 2 tbsp brown sugar - 1 garlic clove minced or crushed - 2 tbsp fresh ginger grated - 1 ½ tbsp soy sauce - 1 tbsp rice wine vinegar - ½ tsp gochugaru (Korean chili flakes) - 2 tsp toasted white sesame seeds
Set aside until ready to use or allow the sauce to cool to room temperature, then refrigerate until ready to use, up to 2 weeks.
When ready to serve, garnish with sesame seeds. - 2 tsp toasted white sesame seeds
For the Alfredo Wings Method
Combine the cheese and butter in the base of a blender. - 4 oz Parmesan cheese finely grated - 2 tbsp unsalted butter
Heat the water and cream in a small sauce pot until simmering. - ½ cup water - ½ cup heavy cream
With the blender running, slowly pour just enough of the heated cream mixture to form a thick sauce. - ½ cup water - ½ cup heavy cream
Use immediately.
